title: Gyárfás-Sumner Conjecture
statement_text: Given two graphs $F_1$ and $F_2$ the class of graphs with no induced $F_1$ or $F_2$ has bounded chromatic number if and only if one of $F_1$, $F_2$ is a complete graph and the other is a forest.
context_text: This conjecture, described as 'tantalizing and still widely open', characterizes the minimal finite families whose induced-subgraph-free classes have bounded chromatic number. The 'only if' direction follows from cliques having unbounded chromatic number and Erdős's high-girth high-chromatic-number construction. The paper extends this interrogation to digraphs via the dichromatic number.
paper_contribution: Proposes Conjecture 4.2 as a digraph analog characterizing heroic sets of size three in terms of dichromatic number, proves the 'only if' direction of that analog (Section 6.1), and establishes positive special cases (Theorems 4.1 and 4.3).
paper_title: Extension of Gyarfas-Sumner conjecture to digraphs

title: Problem 1.2
statement_text: What are the finite sets $\mathcal{F}$ of digraphs for which the class $\mathrm{Forb}_{\mathrm{ind}}(\mathcal{F})$ has bounded dichromatic number?
context_text: Digraphs have no loops or parallel arcs, but both arcs $xy$ and $yx$ (a digon) may be present; an oriented graph is a digraph with at most one arc between any two vertices. The dichromatic number $\vec\chi(D)$ is the minimum number of colours in a colouring of the vertices of $D$ in which no colour class contains a directed cycle (for a graph $G$ seen as the symmetric digraph $\overleftrightarrow{G}$ it equals $\chi(G)$). For a set $\mathcal{F}$ of digraphs, $\mathrm{Forb}_{\mathrm{ind}}(\mathcal{F})$ is the class of digraphs with no member of $\mathcal{F}$ as an induced subdigraph, and $\mathcal{F}$ is heroic if this class has bounded dichromatic number. $\overleftrightarrow{K_2}$ is the digon, $\overrightarrow{K_2}$ the single arc, $\overline{K}_k$ the digraph with $k$ vertices and no arc, and $TT_k$ the transitive tournament on $k$ vertices. A tournament $H$ is a hero if tournaments not containing $H$ have bounded dichromatic number, i.e. $\{\overleftrightarrow{K_2},\overline{K}_2,H\}$ is heroic (note that $\mathrm{Forb}_{\mathrm{ind}}(\overleftrightarrow{K_2},\overline{K}_2)$ is the class of tournaments); Berger, Choromanski, Chudnovsky, Fox, Loebl, Scott, Seymour and Thomassé characterized heroes recursively. The problem is the digraph analogue of the Gyárfás–Sumner question, asking which finite sets of forbidden induced subgraphs bound the chromatic number. A heroic set must contain a complete symmetric digraph $\overleftrightarrow{K_k}$, an oriented forest (an orientation of a forest), a tournament, and a symmetric forest, because of families of digraphs of growing dichromatic number; the unique heroic set of size two is $\{\overleftrightarrow{K_2},\overrightarrow{K_2}\}$. The paper focuses on heroic sets of size three: it shows that for a hero $H$ and $k,\alpha\ge2$, $\{\overleftrightarrow{K_k},\overline{K}_\alpha,H\}$ is heroic if and only if $H$ is transitive or $k=2$, and conjectures a characterization of the heroic sets $\{\overleftrightarrow{K_2},H,F\}$ with $H$ a hero and $F$ an oriented forest.
paper_title: Extension of Gyarfas-Sumner conjecture to digraphs

title: Conjecture 4.2
statement_text: Let $H$ be a hero and let $F$ be an oriented forest. The set $\{\overleftrightarrow{K_2}, H, F\}$ is heroic if and only if: either $F$ is the disjoint union of oriented stars, or $H$ is a transitive tournament.
context_text: Digraphs have no loops or parallel arcs, but both arcs $xy$ and $yx$ (a digon) may be present; an oriented graph is a digraph with at most one arc between any two vertices. The dichromatic number $\vec\chi(D)$ is the minimum number of colours in a colouring of the vertices of $D$ in which no colour class contains a directed cycle (for a graph $G$ seen as the symmetric digraph $\overleftrightarrow{G}$ it equals $\chi(G)$). For a set $\mathcal{F}$ of digraphs, $\mathrm{Forb}_{\mathrm{ind}}(\mathcal{F})$ is the class of digraphs with no member of $\mathcal{F}$ as an induced subdigraph, and $\mathcal{F}$ is heroic if this class has bounded dichromatic number. $\overleftrightarrow{K_2}$ is the digon, $\overrightarrow{K_2}$ the single arc, $\overline{K}_k$ the digraph with $k$ vertices and no arc, and $TT_k$ the transitive tournament on $k$ vertices. A tournament $H$ is a hero if tournaments not containing $H$ have bounded dichromatic number, i.e. $\{\overleftrightarrow{K_2},\overline{K}_2,H\}$ is heroic (note that $\mathrm{Forb}_{\mathrm{ind}}(\overleftrightarrow{K_2},\overline{K}_2)$ is the class of tournaments); Berger, Choromanski, Chudnovsky, Fox, Loebl, Scott, Seymour and Thomassé characterized heroes recursively. An oriented forest is an orientation of a forest, an oriented star is an orientation of a star (a tree with at most one vertex of degree more than 1), and a disjoint union of oriented stars is an oriented forest whose components are oriented stars. Forbidding $\overleftrightarrow{K_2}$ restricts to oriented graphs, so this is a digraph analogue of the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture for oriented graphs. The authors prove the 'only if' direction. When both conditions hold ($H$ transitive and $F$ a disjoint union of oriented stars), Chudnovsky, Scott and Seymour proved that even the chromatic number of the underlying graphs is bounded. As partial evidence the authors prove that $\{\overleftrightarrow{K_2},\vec C_3,\overrightarrow{K_2}+K_1\}$ is heroic, where $\vec C_3$ is the directed triangle and $+$ denotes disjoint union, and that oriented graphs with no induced directed path on 3 arcs and no orientation of $K_4$ have bounded dichromatic number.

title: Conjecture 4.4
statement_text: Given an oriented forest $F$ and for every integer $k$, $\{\overleftrightarrow{K_2}, K_k, F\}$ is heroic.
context_text: Digraphs have no loops or parallel arcs, but both arcs $xy$ and $yx$ (a digon) may be present; an oriented graph is a digraph with at most one arc between any two vertices. The dichromatic number $\vec\chi(D)$ is the minimum number of colours in a colouring of the vertices of $D$ in which no colour class contains a directed cycle (for a graph $G$ seen as the symmetric digraph $\overleftrightarrow{G}$ it equals $\chi(G)$). For a set $\mathcal{F}$ of digraphs, $\mathrm{Forb}_{\mathrm{ind}}(\mathcal{F})$ is the class of digraphs with no member of $\mathcal{F}$ as an induced subdigraph, and $\mathcal{F}$ is heroic if this class has bounded dichromatic number. $\overleftrightarrow{K_2}$ is the digon, $\overrightarrow{K_2}$ the single arc, $\overline{K}_k$ the digraph with $k$ vertices and no arc, and $TT_k$ the transitive tournament on $k$ vertices. A tournament $H$ is a hero if tournaments not containing $H$ have bounded dichromatic number, i.e. $\{\overleftrightarrow{K_2},\overline{K}_2,H\}$ is heroic (note that $\mathrm{Forb}_{\mathrm{ind}}(\overleftrightarrow{K_2},\overline{K}_2)$ is the class of tournaments); Berger, Choromanski, Chudnovsky, Fox, Loebl, Scott, Seymour and Thomassé characterized heroes recursively. Here $K_k$ is the (undirected) complete graph: when an undirected graph is put in the forbidden set, all of its orientations are forbidden, so $\mathrm{Forb}_{\mathrm{ind}}(\overleftrightarrow{K_2},K_k,F)$ is the class of oriented graphs whose underlying graph has clique number less than $k$ and with no induced copy of the oriented forest $F$ (an orientation of a forest). The authors conjecture that, for a hero $H$ and an oriented forest $F$, $\{\overleftrightarrow{K_2},H,F\}$ is heroic if and only if $F$ is a disjoint union of oriented stars or $H$ is a transitive tournament. Since every tournament on at least $2^k$ vertices contains $TT_k$, the special case of that conjecture where $H=TT_k$ for every $k$ is equivalent to this conjecture, which is thus a $\chi$-boundedness-type statement for the dichromatic number of oriented graphs. The authors prove the case $k=4$, $F=P^+(3)$, the directed path with 3 arcs.
notes: PDF source — the raw text reads 'for every integer l' but uses $K_k$ in the set; the variable $l$ is likely a PDF extraction artifact for $k$. Here $K_k$ denotes the independent set (edgeless digraph) on $k$ vertices, as per the paper's notation.

title: Research direction: minimal heroic tournament families
statement_text: Characterize all finite and minimal families $\mathcal{H} = \{H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k\}$ of tournaments such that $\{\overline{K_2}, \overleftrightarrow{K_2}, H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k\}$ is a heroic set.
context_text: Digraphs have no loops or parallel arcs, but both arcs $xy$ and $yx$ (a digon) may be present; an oriented graph is a digraph with at most one arc between any two vertices. The dichromatic number $\vec\chi(D)$ is the minimum number of colours in a colouring of the vertices of $D$ in which no colour class contains a directed cycle (for a graph $G$ seen as the symmetric digraph $\overleftrightarrow{G}$ it equals $\chi(G)$). For a set $\mathcal{F}$ of digraphs, $\mathrm{Forb}_{\mathrm{ind}}(\mathcal{F})$ is the class of digraphs with no member of $\mathcal{F}$ as an induced subdigraph, and $\mathcal{F}$ is heroic if this class has bounded dichromatic number. $\overleftrightarrow{K_2}$ is the digon, $\overrightarrow{K_2}$ the single arc, $\overline{K}_k$ the digraph with $k$ vertices and no arc, and $TT_k$ the transitive tournament on $k$ vertices. A tournament $H$ is a hero if tournaments not containing $H$ have bounded dichromatic number, i.e. $\{\overleftrightarrow{K_2},\overline{K}_2,H\}$ is heroic (note that $\mathrm{Forb}_{\mathrm{ind}}(\overleftrightarrow{K_2},\overline{K}_2)$ is the class of tournaments); Berger, Choromanski, Chudnovsky, Fox, Loebl, Scott, Seymour and Thomassé characterized heroes recursively. Since $\mathrm{Forb}_{\mathrm{ind}}(\overline{K_2},\overleftrightarrow{K_2})$ is the class of tournaments, the question asks for the minimal finite sets of tournaments whose exclusion bounds the dichromatic number of tournaments. The characterization of heroes by Berger et al. settles the case of families of size 1, and implies that a minimal family of size 2 or more cannot contain a hero. Berger et al. also implicitly show that larger minimal heroic sets exist: they identify five tournaments $H_1,\dots,H_5$ (among them $C_3(\overrightarrow{K_2},\overrightarrow{K_2},\overrightarrow{K_2})$ and $C_3(\vec C_3,\vec C_3,K_1)$, where $C_3(D_1,D_2,D_3)$ has all arcs from $D_1$ to $D_2$, from $D_2$ to $D_3$ and from $D_3$ to $D_1$) such that the heroes are exactly the tournaments containing none of them; since every hero is 2-dicolourable, $\{\overline{K_2},\overleftrightarrow{K_2},H_1,\dots,H_5\}$ is heroic, and any minimal heroic subset of it has at least four elements. The authors call the characterization an interesting direction of research.
notes: Expressed as 'an interesting direction of research' in the paper prose, without a formal labelled conjecture or problem environment.
